metric.why: Announced megawatts are the leading indicator for land, power, and equipment demand. The published numbers come almost entirely from commercial research firms; this site links to who publishes them rather than republishing figures it cannot verify.
metric.definition: Capacity in permitting, planned, or under construction per market, the standard unit for comparing data center booms across regions.

reading.body:
Announced megawatt pipelines are the earliest signal of where AI compute will physically exist in 12 to 36 months, making them the most useful leading indicator for land acquisition, power infrastructure, and equipment procurement across regions.

Data center construction announcements precede actual power draw by years. A megawatt in the pipeline today means ground leases, interconnection queue positions, and transformer orders are being placed now. For AI specifically, this metric matters because announced capacity reveals which regions governments and utilities must prioritize for grid upgrades. The power constraint is downstream of this decision, not upstream of it.

These figures come from commercial research firms tracking permitting and construction starts, not from actual operational capacity or signed power contracts. A announced megawatt can be deferred, relocated, or cancelled. The metric also does not distinguish between data center types, utilization rates, or whether announced capacity will actually draw its nameplate power. It shows intent and momentum, not certainty.
